question: does the mask flip because cells sit on the threshold (dither) or because the subject moved?
granularity: dot (2x4 pixel block per cell, one byte per cell)
verdict: BOTH, and that is the actual finding. Flip rate falls monotonically from 67.25% on the threshold to 21.61% far from it (3.1x), so roughly half the raw delta is threshold dither. But the far-from-threshold floor of 21.61% is BELOW the 34.62% independence baseline, so that residual is structured, not noise -- there is genuine change to build on. The tone control came back at 70.91%, WORSE than the mask, so the argmax ramp is not a more stable channel and the fallback is refuted by its own control.
consequence: Two things follow, and the second is the one that matters. First, the fix for the noisy half is hysteresis: keep a dot's bit until its luma crosses the threshold by a margin, not a single bare comparison. The measured gradient sizes it -- a dot more than ~20 counts from the threshold is already 1.6x more stable than one on it, so a margin of that order separates the two populations. Second, the tone channel must NOT be the fallback: at 70.91% it flips more than the mask and carries less stable content. Any P-frame built on tone would be worse, not better.
